name: ONTO
tagline: A founder studio that shows brand, site, app, and CGI work for six projects
description:
ONTO calls itself The Founder Studio. The home page holds a small logo, the line "Design for Disrupters", and one full-width video reel with a Fullscreen button. A Work link leads to the project list.

The work page lists six projects: Select, Microsoft, Vault, Openstore, Science, and Floral. Short labels give the scope, for example brand identity for Select, art direction and CGI for Microsoft, and brand, site, app, motion, 3D, and engineering for Vault. The page also describes a venture studio offer for founders.

The only contact is one email address and two social links. The footer copyright reads 2024.
pricing_detail: No published rates. Contact goes through noa@studio-onto.com.
agent_guidance:
Use it as a reference for a studio home page that lets one video reel carry the brand, with almost no text. The home page HTML holds only a few words, so read /work for the project list.

The site gives no prices, no team, and no location. The footer copyright reads 2024, so make sure the studio is still active before you name it as a current option.
why_it_matters: It shows how far a studio site can reduce text: one reel, one tagline, and one link to the work.
tier_reason: Six named projects with scope labels, among them Microsoft, and a clear one-reel home page. Held at C because the site gives no team, no location, no prices, and no case text in the HTML. The copyright reads 2024, and the site has no sitemap or llms.txt.
notable_for: one full-width video reel on the home page
six projects, including Microsoft and Vault
evidence: Fetched https://studio-onto.com/ and https://studio-onto.com/work with curl on 2026-11-24. Both returned HTTP 200. Home page title "ONTO". The pages read "Design for Disrupters", "The Founder Studio", and "We are a full-service venture studio that founders trust to create products that become verbs". https://studio-onto.com/llms.txt 404 and https://studio-onto.com/sitemap.xml 404. The page is static HTML with Barba.js markup and a Lottie script, and it shows no framework markers.

name: 9.8 agency

description:

The services list covers producing, strategy, branding, web, campaigns, communications, and illustration. The page shows five cases: Borscht Collective, People of February (Люди лютого), S&PLB, James Blond, and Athena. Each case includes naming or identity work, and some also include a website. Borscht Collective collects food trucks for the Ukrainian army, and Athena supports Ukrainian women with cancer.

The site states no prices. Contact goes through yo@9point8.agency, Telegram, and a phone number with the +380 Ukraine code.
pricing_detail: No published rates. Contact goes through yo@9point8.agency or Telegram.
agent_guidance:
Use it as a reference for a one-page agency site set almost fully in large type, with a bilingual text system. One scroll carries the services, the founder note, and five cases.

The cases are mostly naming and identity work for Ukrainian clients and causes. Read them for brand-system examples, not for product design. The site has no sitemap and no llms.txt, and it states no prices.
why_it_matters: It shows how a small agency puts its services, its founder, and its cases on one page in two languages.
tier_reason: Five cases with real clients, a clear service list, and a 2026 copyright. Held at C because all work sits on one page with short case text, the page names only the founder, and the site has no prices, no sitemap, and no llms.txt.

naming and identity for Ukrainian causes
founder with 14 years of visual work

name: hellohello
tagline: Montevideo agency for brand, product design, and engineering, with an llms.txt and Markdown pages
description:
++hellohello is a design and technology agency with its headquarters in Montevideo, Uruguay. It also lists team members in San Francisco, New York, Toronto, and London. Its llms.txt says that Rafael Cavestany, Pablo Picart, and Sebastián Martínez started it on May 8, 2017. The work connects branding, product design, and engineering, and the engineering list names React, Next.js, TypeScript, Framer, and Webflow.

The home page features four cases: the AI in Design Report 2026 for Designer Fund, Passkeys Developer Kit, Grateful by Exodus, and Alchemy. The llms.txt lists nine case studies with stated results, including Constructor.io and AstroPay, and work with Jam3 for Meta, Adidas, and Google. The awards list includes 9 Awwwards, 4 FWA, 2 Framer Awards, and an Awwwards Studio of the Year nomination in November 2025.

The site publishes an llms.txt, an llms-full.txt, and a Markdown copy of each page. It states no prices.
pricing_detail: No published rates. The contact form asks for the company, the role, and the service, and the email is hi@hellohello.is.
agent_guidance:
Read https://www.hellohello.is/llms.txt first. It lists every case study with the year, the scope, and the stated results. Add .md to a page URL, or send Accept: text/markdown, to get a clean Markdown copy.

Use it as a benchmark for an agency that sells brand, product, and engineering as one service to fintech, Web3, and AI companies. The result figures come from the agency itself, so cite them as claims.
why_it_matters: It is a studio site that an agent can read in full, through llms.txt and Markdown pages, next to a dated awards list and named client results.
tier_reason: Nine case studies with named clients and stated results, a dated awards list with 9 Awwwards and a Studio of the Year nomination, and an llms.txt with Markdown copies of each page. Held below S because the result figures are self-reported and the site states no prices.

brand, product design, and engineering in one team

name: Chipsa

description:

name: Pixels Studio
tagline: Practice of Abhishek Kambli, a product designer and frontend engineer for AI and SaaS
description:
Pixels Studio is the independent practice of Abhishek Kambli, a product designer and frontend engineer. The page title uses his name, and the text speaks in the first person. He states over a decade of work on AI, communication, and enterprise SaaS products. He also leads product design and frontend direction at Samespace.

The work list holds eight products: Origon, Samespace, Hub, Resolve, Tlkn, Tribe, Prism, and Rhythm, plus a playground of experiments. Each entry has a one-line caption and its own screen pages. Prism and Rhythm are his own browser tools on subdomains.

The services section shows two offers: a product design sprint from $2,500 and ongoing support from $5,000 a month. The site publishes an llms.txt and a sitemap with 34 URLs.
pricing_detail: Product design sprint from $2,500. Ongoing product support from $5,000 a month. The llms.txt calls the sprint a 2-week, one-time engagement.
agent_guidance:
Treat it as a designer portfolio, not a studio. One person does the work, and the page says he is also open to full-time remote roles.

Read /llms.txt for the services and the selected projects in plain text. Use the /m/ screen pages in the sitemap to see the product UI for Origon, Hub, Resolve, and Tribe.
why_it_matters: It shows a product designer who also ships frontend code, with prices, screen pages, and an llms.txt on one small site.
tier_reason: Eight products with screen pages, two priced offers, a named client testimonial, and an llms.txt. Held at B because the projects have captions and screens but no written case studies, and only one client quote is on the page.
notable_for: product design and frontend engineering by one person

name: Eleveight Studio

description:

The services cover web design, development, website migration, custom integrations, UI and UX, and ongoing optimization. The sectors are AI, SaaS, eCommerce, fintech, automotive, and real estate. Seven testimonials name clients such as warp.dev, Visual Electric, and pillar.io. The page says that Framer vetted Fabian as a Pro Expert and an Enterprise Partner.

The prices are on the page: $10K for a landing page, $20K for a full website, and $8K a month for a retainer.

Use it as a reference for a small Framer studio that publishes fixed prices and sells async work. The price block and the FAQ give a clear model for a small service offer.

The home page shows client sites as full-page screenshots, not as written case studies. The sitemap lists only the root URL, and the site has no llms.txt.

name: Ouro Labs
tagline: Design and AI practice of two design leaders, who build their own apps and agent workflows
description:
Ouro Labs calls itself a design and AI practice built by two design leaders, and its page title says AI-Native Product Studio. The home page states that it explores design, code, systems, and AI through practice, not theory. Its values are play, precision, and craft.

The page shows three of its own projects, not client work. Nota is a native app to review video footage and log moments. It is in testing, with an App Store launch expected by summer 2026. Overture DS is a workflow to shape design systems with agents, with JSON and YAML for machines and a DESIGN_SYSTEM.MD file for people. Health Atlas is a personal experiment that uses AI to organize health records.

The site publishes an llms.txt that tells AI systems how to describe the practice, and a sitemap with two URLs. It states no prices.
pricing_detail: No services or rates on the home page. Contact goes through hello@ourolabs.com and LinkedIn.
agent_guidance:
Read it for the Overture DS idea: a design system that agents read through JSON and YAML, with a DESIGN_SYSTEM.MD file for the human rationale. This is a described workflow, not a released tool.

Do not list it as an agency for hire. The page shows only the practice's own projects, with no client work and no prices. Read /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt for the practice's own summary.
why_it_matters: It shows two design leaders who present their own apps and agent workflows as the portfolio, instead of client cases.
tier_reason: A clear position on design, code, and AI, three described projects, and an llms.txt. Held at C because no project is publicly launched, the site shows no client work or prices, and the home page does not name the two founders.
notable_for: Overture DS: design systems with agents

name: VibeFlow
tagline: Subscription design studio for startup sites in Framer and Webflow, from $4,999 a month
description:
VibeFlow calls itself a tiny design and development studio. It sells design to startup founders at a flat monthly rate, with a focus on Web3, SaaS, AI, tech, and creative brands. It designs in Figma and builds in Framer or Webflow.

The services are marketing sites, landing pages, web apps, mobile apps, motion design, alternative interfaces, and pitch decks. The Lite plan costs $4,999 a month for one active request. The Unlimited plan costs $7,999 a month. The FAQ says that each client gets a project board in Linear.

The testimonials include one attributed to "Steve Jobs, Founder at Apple", which is a placeholder. Another testimonial names a different studio, Morva. The site shows no case studies.
pricing_detail: Lite: $4,999 a month, one active request, a landing page and marketing design. Unlimited: $7,999 a month, up to 10 pages and all types of design requests. A project-based plan is available on request.
agent_guidance:
Use it as a reference for a subscription design offer with a plain monospace layout and a two-plan price table.

Do not cite the testimonials as client proof. One is attributed to Steve Jobs at Apple, and another praises a different studio, Morva. The site has no case studies, no llms.txt, and a sitemap with only the home page and a 404 page.
why_it_matters: It shows the subscription design model in its smallest form: two monthly plans, a Linear board for requests, and a Framer or Webflow build.
tier_reason: Clear subscription prices and a full service list. Held at C because the testimonials include a placeholder quote from Steve Jobs, the site shows no case studies, and the sitemap lists only two URLs.

Every testimonial names one designer, Himanshu. The work section lists non-NDA projects such as Wise Counsel, Medflick, Twire.gg, and RemoteNomad, and the full portfolio opens as a Figma prototype.

The price table shows a landing page plan at $3000+ and $4800+, and a multi-page plan at $5000+ and $8000+. No-code development costs $1800 or $3000 more. The HTML holds two figures for each plan and does not label the difference.
